concerns.text: Task T035a defines 'high-yield' as a 'global constant' calculated on the ENTIRE dataset, then checks frequency in the SC-003 held-out set. This violates SC-003 which requires validating that substructures are present in >80% of high-yield reactions 'within a held-out validation set'. Using global statistics to define the threshold introduces data leakage (the threshold depends on data outside the validation set) and fails to measure the specific criterion defined in the spec.

Task T022e creates a fourth disjoint set ('SC-003 Held-Out Validation Set') by excluding Train, Val, and Test groups. FR-004 and Constitution Principle VI mandate a single stratified split (Train/Val/Test) to prevent leakage. Creating a disjoint fourth set risks leaving insufficient data for the primary validation/test sets and contradicts the 'scaffold-based split' strategy defined in the spec and plan.

Task T033 maps bits to 'reactant/reagent' substructures but fails to explicitly identify and distinguish the 'reaction center' (specific atoms involved in the chemical transformation) as required by FR-008. The task aggregates importance across general substructures without isolating the reaction center, weakening the deliverable against the spec's requirement to map bits to 'reaction centers and associated substructures'.

Task T022a implements a heuristic to assign 'primary classes' to cross-class scaffolds. FR-004 only specifies a 'scaffold-based split (grouping by reactant core)' without authorizing this specific heuristic. Assigning cross-class scaffolds to a primary class introduces a bias not accounted for in the spec's acceptance criteria, potentially weakening the constraint of preventing data leakage via strict scaffold grouping.
